scenario: Community search over short user-generated posts, questions and comments. Focus: relevance, CTR, semantic matching, query understanding, retrieval and ranking.

papers.title: E8-QAT: Efficient 2-Bit Quantization-Aware Training with Implicit Lattice Codebooks
papers.authors: Xinyu Lei, Hong Huang, Jiebin Zhang, Hongyu Li, Jinlong Song, Decheng Wu, Guanghua Yu, Jianchen Zhu, Sujian Li
papers.summary: Grouped weight quantization avoids an explicit codebook search by projecting onto a structured lattice. At each format’s largest feasible batch, decoding reaches 1.97 times BF16 throughput. This comparison includes the batch-size benefit of lower memory use.
papers.key_insight: Treat storage format and feasible batch size as coupled decisions. Arithmetic lattice projection reduces codebook search overhead, while memory savings create additional serving capacity.

papers.title: Large Flow Language Models
papers.authors: Arnav Chavan, Chanhyuk Lee, Udbhav Bamba, Jaehoon Yoo, Seunghoon Hong
papers.summary: Lafa adapts pretrained autoregressive models into blockwise continuous-flow language models. A single model proposes flow-based drafts and verifies them autoregressively, reaching 2.54 times autoregressive throughput at comparable quality.
papers.key_insight: Drafting and verification can share a model. Retaining autoregressive capability creates a verification path for parallel flow proposals without a separately maintained drafter.

papers.title: Reconstruction-Optimized Expert Pruning for Mixture-of-Experts Language Models
papers.authors: Jelena Markovic-Voronov, Petros Prastakos, Kayhan Behdin, Jincheng Cao, Zhipeng Wang, Shayan Mohajer Hamidi, Yuanda Xu, Zhengze Zhou, Wenhui Zhu, Rahul Mazumder
papers.summary: OptEP selects expert subsets by reconstructing each original layer’s output, then lightly adapts the retained weights. On Qwen3-30B-A3B it improves accuracy by up to 15.05 percentage points over the strongest expert-pruning baseline.
papers.key_insight: Optimize the expert subset as a whole. Reconstruction captures complementary contributions that independent popularity rankings can miss, and retained-weight adaptation helps after aggressive pruning.

papers.title: Beyond 4 bits: Data-Centric Post-training Quantization and Recovery
papers.authors: Rhea Sanjay Sukthanker, Riccardo Grazzi, James Hensman, Pashmina Cameron
papers.summary: The study jointly tunes vector-codebook representation, calibration data and recovery data for very low-bit compression. Codebook-only recovery retains 89–97% of full-precision QA accuracy in settings where scalar quantization falls to chance.
papers.key_insight: Calibration and recovery data interact. At low bit widths, evaluate the pair together and inspect generative tasks separately, because aggregate QA scores hide uneven capability losses.

papers.title: RouterWorld: Scaling Conversational AI with Latency-Aware LLM Routing
papers.authors: Jinyang Li, Denis Emelin, Simone Tedeschi, Weiwei Cheng, Cristina Morariu, Haytham Assem, Jens Lehmann, Emine Yilmaz, Angus Addlesee
papers.summary: RouterWorld evaluates model routing with partial feedback and hardware-grounded latency labels. Across 13 baselines, routers tend to favor accuracy while neglecting latency; the benchmark includes static cold-start logs and a streaming setting.
papers.key_insight: A router changes the data it will observe next. Evaluate that feedback loop instead of assuming every candidate model’s answer is available for training and scoring.

papers.title: MLIPS: Multi-Layer Indexer Pool Sharing
papers.authors: Samkit Jain, Sai Kishan Pampana, Shlok Agarwal
papers.summary: MLIPS shares a broad candidate pool across sparse-attention layers while preserving each layer’s own final selection. A vLLM implementation reports 1.14–1.40 times speedup on long-context suites; broader sharing incurs task-dependent quality losses.
papers.key_insight: Reuse candidate discovery rather than forcing identical attention selections. Broad pools can cover different layers’ needs even when their final selections overlap little.

papers.title: Factorization-Guided Training and Inference for Diffusion-Drafted Speculative Decoding
papers.authors: Jiakun Fan, Min Xiao, Qiang Wang, Neiwen Ling, Zhichao Liu, Zhihao Jia, Dimitrios S. Nikolopoulos, Zijun Wei
papers.summary: DScout aligns diffusion-drafter training with contiguous-prefix acceptance and tunes inference using accepted tokens per round divided by round latency. It reports a mean 4.14 times speedup over autoregressive decoding on Qwen3-8B.
papers.key_insight: A better drafter is not necessarily a faster system. Optimize accepted-prefix yield together with round latency, and choose draft depth and block size for the actual concurrency regime.

papers.title: Meta Expert: Cross-Layer Expert Sharing for Storage- and Retrieval-Efficient MoE
papers.authors: Ermo Hua, Xiangyu Hong, Baiting Wu, Che Jiang, Haozheng Hou, Yicheng Gu, Hanjing Wang, Qirui Zeng, Ming Zhang, Ning Ding, Qipeng Guo, Youbang Sun, Biqing Qi, Bowen Zhou
papers.summary: Meta Expert shares experts across layers to reduce duplicated parameters. With activation count and expert granularity fixed, the model matches a conventional MoE using 70–80% as many experts.
papers.key_insight: Cross-layer reuse changes how storage is allocated across capabilities. It is an architectural training choice, so compare its adoption cost separately from post-training expert pruning.

papers.title: Retrofitting language models to operate over bytes
papers.summary: Byteification retrofits pretrained subword models to operate on bytes using learned byte patches around the existing backbone. The conversion uses less than 1% of a typical pretraining budget.
papers.key_insight: Reuse a mature backbone when exploring alternative text representations. Byte-level adaptation can focus training on patch boundaries and fine-grained character behavior instead of rebuilding the entire pretraining pipeline.

papers.title: Amazon DynamoDB now supports real-time vector search at any scale
papers.summary: DynamoDB adds native vector indexing and filtered similarity search beside operational records, removing a separate replication pipeline. AWS claims recall above 99%; the announcement does not provide a full comparative benchmark.
papers.key_insight: Co-locating vectors with operational records reduces synchronization work. This is most relevant when the application already uses DynamoDB; assess filters, update rates and query volume in the cost comparison.
